module_title: The 7 Layers of OSI, Routers, and Modems
introduction: This intermediate tier requires you to memorize the exact sequence of the 7 OSI layers. We will also analyze the most critical internet devices: 'Routers' and 'Modems', which are heavily tested in SSC and Banking exams.

core_concepts.title: The 7 Layers of OSI (Bottom to Top)
core_concepts.description:
1. Physical Layer
2. Data Link Layer
3. Network Layer
4. Transport Layer
5. Session Layer
6. Presentation Layer
7. Application Layer (The top layer where users interact, e.g., Web Browsers).

core_concepts.title: Router
core_concepts.description: The most important internet device. While Hubs and Switches connect computers within the SAME network, a Router connects completely DIFFERENT networks together (e.g., connecting your home LAN to the massive internet WAN). It uses 'IP Addresses' to find the shortest and fastest route for data to travel.

core_concepts.title: Modem (Modulator-Demodulator)
core_concepts.description: Computers only understand Digital signals (0s and 1s), but telephone/cable lines carry Analog signals. A Modem 'Modulates' digital data into analog for transmission, and 'Demodulates' incoming analog signals back into digital data for the computer.

important_entities.name: Bridge
important_entities.significance: A networking device used to connect two 'Similar' Local Area Networks together to form one larger, extended LAN.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A classic exam trap: 'Which device is used to connect two different networks?' Many candidates guess Switch. Wrong! A Switch only manages devices inside ONE network. To connect TWO DIFFERENT networks, you strictly need a Router.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: P (Physical) -> D (Data Link) -> N (Network) -> T (Transport) -> S (Session) -> P (Presentation) -> A (Application). This ensures you remember the exact bottom-to-top sequence.

exam_strategy_tips: The full form of MODEM (Modulator-Demodulator) is a staple question across all competitive exams. Ensure you know its exact spelling.
